title: Rookies Worth a Look
brief: Which rookies have a real path to minutes and usage this season, and which belong only in the 1 USD flyer zone or on waivers? It must reflect that most rookie classes give only a few relevant players and that rookie guards usually shoot poorly early.
summary: Only two rookies are worth real auction money in our league: Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson. Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa, Darius Acuff Jr. and Yaxel Lendeborg are cheap late flyers. Almost everyone else in the class belongs on a waiver watch list. Expect rookie guards to hurt FG% and TO early, so do not pay for draft slot or name.

paragraphs.text: Do not overrate rookies. At best a class gives one top 50 player and three top 100 players. Drafters take far too many rookies near the end of drafts, while most classes give only three or four relevant players. In our 144-player auction, plan for only three or four rookies to matter across all 12 rosters.

Judge a rookie by his situation, minutes, usage and non-scoring stats, not by where he was drafted. The No. 1 overall pick, AJ Dybantsa, is a good example. The experts value him at about 1 USD. Cameron Boozer is the No. 1 rookie for fantasy this season.

sections.heading: The two rookies worth real money

paragraphs.text: Boozer is the one rookie to target with real money. The experts' fair range is around rank 60 to 65. That fits a price near the 15 USD mock price, not Yahoo's 18 USD value. He is expected to play at a top 35 level in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. He also has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule with few back-to-backs. He fits punt TO builds. In the first weeks, check his minutes in Iisalo's short-stint rotation and how many threes he takes.

Caleb Wilson is the second rookie worth buying. He is a defense-first forward whose blocks and rebounds carry his value. His FT% and his threes are mild drags. The experts put him in the 80s overall, which makes him a mid-to-late pick at about Yahoo's 11 USD value. Buy him for a blocks-and-rebounds build that can absorb a weak FT%. Early on, check his usage next to Powell, Giddey and Buzelis.

Dybantsa is not in this group. His projected line is close to neutral except for points, plus a drag on turnovers. He only makes sense as a 1 to 2 USD bench piece for a punt TO build. Let another manager pay for the No. 1 pick name. Check whether he plays 28 minutes or 34 plus, and how many shots he gets next to Trae Young and Anthony Davis.

Rookie point guards are almost always bad for fantasy because of efficiency problems. Be skeptical of them in redraft. FG% is a team ratio in our league, so a rookie guard who takes a lot of shots does the most damage. Darius Acuff Jr. projects to 42.6% FG on about 14 shots a game with 2.5 turnovers. He is a last-dollar flyer, and only for a team that already plans to give up FG% and TO for points and assists.

Darryn Peterson is the best of the rookie guards for us. The experts see him as a late pick around 110 to 130. That makes him fine as a bench upside piece at 2 to 5 USD, and not worth more. His projection is about average in every category, but expect poor FG% and turnovers early. Check whether he starts and how many minutes he gets next to George, Markkanen and Jackson Jr.

Mikel Brown Jr., Keaton Wagler, Kingston Flemings and Brayden Burries should not cost auction money. Brown is at most a 1 USD last bench pick. He is more likely a waiver add if he starts at point guard and his assists and steals show up. He has only 10 games in our playoff weeks. Wagler projects as a backup point guard with efficiency problems. Flemings and Burries have no strong category.

sections.heading: The flyer zone and the two-week rule

paragraphs.text: Uncertain rookies belong around picks 120 to 130 in a 12-team league. That is the end of the active roster or the start of the bench. In our auction, that means your last 1 to 2 USD spots. Yaxel Lendeborg fits that zone, and so do Morez Johnson Jr. and Hannes Steinbach at 1 USD. Only take Steinbach if Charlotte names him a starter before the 2026-10-18 auction.

Use Summer League and preseason news. If a rookie is named a starter, move him up your list. If nothing happens in his first two weeks, drop him and maybe pick him up later. Lendeborg was the 2026 Summer League MVP. Check whether Kerr keeps him in the starting lineup, and plan to drop or trade him before Butler and Moody return. For Johnson, check his lower leg injury and the Lively timeline before the draft. Then watch whether Dusty May starts him over Gafford.

We have a cap of 6 acquisitions per week, so keep a short list of injury triggers rather than chasing every name. Flemings matters only if McCollum misses time and Flemings, not Dort or Wiggins, gets the minutes. Christian Anderson matters if he becomes the backup point guard while Coby White is out. Ryan Conwell matters if he plays ahead of Dru Smith. Sergio de Larrea matters if he gets assists on nights Kyrie sits. Aday Mara matters if Hartenstein or Holmgren misses games. For Burries, check the Bucks' guard minutes after the 2027-03-04 trade deadline.

Two-way players with a 50 game limit can still be worth a roster spot late in the season when they play. Jalen Slawson is worth an add if he gets about 20 minutes a night, because of his steals and blocks. Ugonna Onyenso is a fast add if Duren or Reed misses time. Javon Small only matters if he gets a standard contract or a Memphis guard gets hurt.

Some rookies are out of our season. Henri Veesaar is out for the season with a torn ACL. Richie Saunders is expected back only near the end of his rookie season, likely after our 2027-03-28 finish, so he is not an IL stash. Jayden Quaintance is out after another knee surgery with no firm return date.

The market and the experts disagree on several top rookies. On one side, Yahoo and ESPN put Dybantsa near rank 90, and ESPN ranks Wilson 57. On the other side, the experts value Dybantsa at about 1 USD and put Wilson in the 80s. The projections also split on threes. Yahoo gives Boozer and Lendeborg 1.3 threes a game, while ESPN gives each of them 0.3. For Johnson, the FG% projections are 58.9 and 49.4. Follow the expert prices in the auction. Then let the first weeks of three-point volume decide whether Boozer and Lendeborg help or hurt your 3PM.
